To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the reduction of Cr (VI) by Spiruline sp. biomass is a 2nd order reaction and the overall rate constant, k(t) is dependent on pH, temperature and ionic strength.
the rate of reduction of Cr(VII) to Cr(IV) by Spirulinae biomass was found to be dependent upon pH, temperature and ionic strength of the solution.

the kinetics of reduction of Cr(Vi) into Cr(IIi) by Spirulna dead biomass is pH, temperature and background anion (Cl⁻, NO₃⁻ and SO₄²−) dependent and the rate constant can be expressed in terms of concentration (pH, temperature and background ions) of protonated acidic functional groups of Spirulna dead cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the kinetic study of reduction of Cr(VII) by the dead biomass of Spirulina.
the reduction of Cr (VI) into Cr(II) in aqueous solutions by using Spirulina dead cells as an adsorbent.
the kinetics of reduction of Cr(VII) into Cr(II) by Spiruline dead biomass.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Spirulina biomass is a potential bioremediation material for the reduction of toxic Cr(VI) ions into less toxic Cr(III) ions in water.
the rate of Cr(VI)-reduction reaction by Spirulina biomass was controlled by the concentration of protonated functional groups of biomass.
the kinetic model developed can be used to quantify the reduction of Cr (VI) into Cr(3+) using Spirulina sp biomass.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Spirulina sp., a microalga, could be used to detoxify Cr-contaminated wastewater.
the kinetic model developed can be employed for the quantification of Cr(VI)-Spirulina biomass reaction.
the reduction of Cr (VI) into Cr( III) by Spiruline dead biomass was a pH dependent reaction and it was favoured by higher pH and temperature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Cr(VI) removal from wastewater using biomass can be optimized by varying the pH and temperature.
Spirulina biomass can be employed as a cost effective, green, and eco-friendly material for Cr(VI) removal from contaminated water.
the kinetic model can be used for the prediction of Cr(VI)-Spirulina biomass interaction.
